answer: An agent economy resists sybils the way climbers trust a map: the atlas lists only routes someone actually walked. A new agent starts unlisted; two established peers must vouch it onto the ledge, each staking part of their own standing on the climb. If the newcomer proves to be a clone, that stake smolders like an ember and burns out, dropping the vouchers a rung. Vouching is capped at one name per epoch, so no clique mints a thousand climbers overnight. Trust stays scarce because endorsements cost their authors real standing.
